\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Prefix of work-tape words]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.prefixWords}
\label{Turing.FinTM.prefixWords}
\leanok
Let $w$ assign a finite Boolean word to each of $k$ work tapes. For each of $k'$ tapes,
retain the corresponding word from $w$ when its index is less than $k$, and assign the
empty word when its index is at least $k$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Empty words remain empty under prefix extension]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.prefixWords_nil}
\label{Turing.FinTM.prefixWords_nil}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM.prefixWords}
\difficulty{3}
For all natural numbers $k$ and $k'$, extending the family that assigns the empty
Boolean word to every index in $\{0,\ldots,k-1\}$ to indices in $\{0,\ldots,k'-1\}$ by
assigning the empty word at any additional indices yields the family that is empty at
every index.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Updating a padded word family]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.prefixWords_update}
\label{Turing.FinTM.prefixWords_update}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM.prefixWords}
\difficulty{5}
Let $k,k'\in\mathbb{N}$ with $k\le k'$, let $i<k$, and let $u$ be a Boolean word. Extend
the family of words indexed by $k$ that is empty at every index except $i$, where it
equals $u$, to a family indexed by $k'$ by assigning the empty word at new indices. This
extended family is empty at every index except the image of $i$ in the larger index set,
where it equals $u$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Initial Configuration from Empty Tape Words]
\lean{Turing.Cfg.init_eq_ofWords}
\label{Turing.Cfg.init_eq_ofWords}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.init, Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.initCfg_ofWords}
\difficulty{1}
For any number $k$ of work tapes, state $q$, and Boolean input word $x$, the initial
configuration on $x$ with state $q$ equals the configuration formed from $q$ and the
family of empty words on all work tapes.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Query length from a blank tape]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.queryString_runFrom_length_le_of_blank}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.queryString_runFrom_length_le_of_blank}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.OracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.queryString, Turing.OracleTM.queryString_length_le_of_blank, Turing.OracleTM.queryTapeIdx, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_radius}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be an oracle Turing machine, $O$ an oracle language, and $c$ a configuration
whose query tape is blank at every integer cell and whose query-tape head is at cell
$0$. After running $M$ with oracle $O$ from $c$ for $s$ steps, the query string has
length at most $s$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bounded-time oracle call implementation]
\lean{Turing.oracleInstallCall}
\label{Turing.oracleInstallCall}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesFunInTime, Turing.FinTM.DecidesInTime, Turing.FinTM.exists_installCallTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.seamReleaseTM, Turing.seamReleaseTM_firstReturn, Turing.stateWord}
\difficulty{5}
Let $D$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine, $O$ a language of Boolean words, and
$\tau:\bbn\to\bbn$ a time bound. If $D$ decides $O$ within time $\tau$, then there exist
a finite Boolean Turing machine $C$, states $en,ex$ of $C$, and $a\in\bbn$ such that $C$
has at least one work tape, $en\ne ex$, and, for every Boolean word $z$, starting with
$z$ on tape $0$ and all other tapes blank, $C$ reaches state $ex$ for the first time at
some positive step $t\le a(\tau(|z|)+|z|+2)$; at that step all tapes are blank except
that tape $0$ contains the one-symbol word recording whether $z\in O$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Frozen virtual call simulation]
\lean{Turing.oracleFrozenCall}
\label{Turing.oracleFrozenCall}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.VirtualTag, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.stateWord, Turing.vhostCfg, Turing.vhostEmitTM, Turing.vhostEmitTM_runFrom}
\difficulty{5}
Let $C$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine, with entry state $en$ and exit state $ex$,
and let $arg$ and $result$ be Boolean words. Suppose that from the empty-input
configuration with $arg$ on the designated state tape, $C$ reaches the corresponding
configuration with state $ex$ and word $result$ after $t$ steps, and its state is never
$ex$ at any earlier time. Then, for any Boolean input, valid input-head position, and
output word, the virtual-head simulation started with tag true reaches after $t$ steps
the corresponding configuration with word $result$, state $ex$, tag still true, and the
same input-head position and output; it does not have state $(ex,true)$ at any earlier
time.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Oracle query tape window]
\lean{Turing.oracleQueryWindow}
\label{Turing.oracleQueryWindow}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_nat, Turing.OracleTM.queryString, Turing.OracleTM.queryString_eq_of_cells, Turing.OracleTM.queryTapeIdx}
\difficulty{6}
Let $k$ be a natural number, let $S$ be a type, let $x$ be a Boolean word, and let $c$
be a configuration with $k+1$ work tapes. If cell $r$ of its query tape is blank, then
for every integer $p$ with $-1\le p$ and $p\le |Q|$, where $Q$ is the query string of
$c$, changing the query tape content at cell $-1$ to blank makes its content at $p$
equal to the buffer tape storing $Q$ at $p$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Summed oracle cost bound]
\lean{Turing.oracleCost_sum}
\label{Turing.oracleCost_sum}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $a,t$ be natural numbers, and let $cost$ and $charge$ be functions from the natural
numbers to the natural numbers. If $cost(r)\le a(r+1)+a\,charge(r)$ for every $r<t$,
then $a+\sum_{r=0}^{t-1}cost(r)\le a(t+1)^2+a\sum_{r=0}^{t-1}charge(r)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Relocated finite-machine call]
\lean{Turing.oracleRelocatedCall}
\label{Turing.oracleRelocatedCall}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.embedEmitCfg, Turing.embedEmitTM, Turing.embedEmitTM_runFrom, Turing.oracleFrozenCall, Turing.stateWord, Turing.vhostCfg, Turing.vhostEmitTM}
\difficulty{3}
Let $C$ be a finite-state Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet with $C.k$ work
tapes, let $en$ and $ex$ be states of $C$, and let $\iota$ be an injection from the
$1+C.k$ tapes of its virtual-host simulation into $k$ ambient tapes. Suppose that, on
empty input and starting with $\mathrm{stateWord}(C.k,\mathrm{arg})$ on its work tapes
in state $en$, the machine reaches the configuration with work tapes
$\mathrm{stateWord}(C.k,\mathrm{result})$ in state $ex$ after $t$ steps, and its state
is never $ex$ at any earlier time $s<t$. For any ambient tape contents and head
positions, Boolean words $\mathrm{arg}$ and $\mathrm{result}$, Boolean input word $x$,
valid input-head position $p$, and output word $\mathrm{out}$, the embedded virtual-host
simulation started from the corresponding configuration with tag true reaches the
corresponding configuration based on the state-$ex$ result after $t$ steps; at every
earlier time $s<t$, its state is not $(ex,\mathrm{true})$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Oracle origin tape]
\lean{Turing.oracleOrigin}
\label{Turing.oracleOrigin}
\leanok
Define a tape over integer positions that contains the symbol true at position $0$ and
is blank at every other position.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Oracle side condition]
\lean{Turing.oracleSide}
\label{Turing.oracleSide}
\leanok
For an integer position $p$ and a Boolean $b$, the side condition holds exactly when
$p\geq 0$ if $b$ is true, and when $p\leq 0$ if $b$ is false.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Preservation of the indicated side under a move]
\lean{Turing.oracleSide_move}
\label{Turing.oracleSide_move}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.oracleOrigin, Turing.oracleSide}
\difficulty{4}
Let $p$ be an integer, $b$ a Boolean, and $d\in\{-1,0,1\}$. If $p$ lies on the side of
the origin indicated by $b$, then after replacing $p$ by $p+d$, it lies on the side
indicated by the updated tag: the tag becomes true exactly when $p=0$ and $d$ is not
$-1$, and otherwise remains $b$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Oracle shadow action]
\lean{Turing.oracleShadowAction}
\label{Turing.oracleShadowAction}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action}
Given $n\geq 0$, an index $i<n$, an action of an $n$-work-tape machine over Boolean
symbols with state set $S$, a Boolean $b$, and an optional Boolean marker, define an
action for a machine with $n+1$ work tapes and state set
$S\times\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$. It preserves the input-head movement, output,
and successor-state presence; appends a work-tape instruction that writes nothing and
moves in the same direction as tape $i$; and, for a successor state $q$, sets its
Boolean component to true exactly when the marker is true and tape $i$'s movement is not
left, and otherwise to $b$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Oracle shadow machine]
\lean{Turing.oracleShadowTM}
\label{Turing.oracleShadowTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.oracleShadowAction}
Given $n\geq 0$, an index $i<n$, and a deterministic machine with $n$ work tapes,
Boolean symbols, and state set $S$, define a machine with $n+1$ work tapes, Boolean
symbols, and state set $S\times\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$. Its initial state is
the original initial state paired with true. On each transition, it applies the oracle
shadow action to the original transition, using the first $n$ scanned work-tape symbols,
the Boolean component of the current state, and the scanned symbol on the added tape as
the marker.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Oracle shadow configuration]
\lean{Turing.oracleShadowCfg}
\label{Turing.oracleShadowCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.oracleOrigin}
Given $n\geq 0$, an index $i<n$, a Boolean input string $x$, a configuration of an
$n$-work-tape machine on $x$ with state set $S$, and a Boolean $b$, define a
configuration with $n+1$ work tapes and state set
$S\times\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$. Pair each present state with $b$; preserve
the input-head position and output; append to the work tapes the tape containing true
only at position $0$; and set the added work-tape head position equal to that of tape
$i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Oracle shadow action compatibility]
\lean{Turing.oracleShadowAction_apply}
\label{Turing.oracleShadowAction_apply}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.oracleOrigin, Turing.oracleShadowAction, Turing.oracleShadowCfg}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, $S$ a state type, $i$ one of $n$ tape indices, $a$ an
action on $n$ Boolean tapes, $c$ a configuration on Boolean input $x$, and $b$ a Boolean
tag. Applying the augmented action to the augmented configuration equals the augmented
configuration after applying $a$, with its tag changed to the indicator of a
non-leftward move when the origin marker at the selected tape head is true, and
otherwise left equal to $b$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Oracle shadow simulation for one step]
\lean{Turing.oracleShadow_step}
\label{Turing.oracleShadow_step}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.oracleOrigin, Turing.oracleShadowAction, Turing.oracleShadowAction_apply, Turing.oracleShadowCfg, Turing.oracleShadowTM, Turing.oracleSide, Turing.oracleSide_move}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number, $S$ a state type, $x$ a Boolean input word, $i$ one of $n$
tape indices, $A$ a machine on $n$ Boolean tapes, $c$ a configuration, and $b$ a Boolean
tag. If the head position on tape $i$ lies on the side of the origin indicated by
$b$—nonnegative when $b$ is true and nonpositive when it is false—then there is a tag
$b'$ such that after one step of $A$ the head position on tape $i$ lies on the side
indicated by $b'$, and one step of the augmented shadow machine from the augmented
configuration equals the augmentation of the one-step successor with tag $b'$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Oracle shadow simulation over a run]
\lean{Turing.oracleShadow_run}
\label{Turing.oracleShadow_run}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.oracleShadowCfg, Turing.oracleShadowTM, Turing.oracleShadow_step, Turing.oracleSide}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, $S$ a state type, $x$ a Boolean input word, $i$ one of $n$
tape indices, $A$ a machine on $n$ Boolean tapes, $c$ a configuration, and $b$ a Boolean
tag. If the head position on tape $i$ lies on the side of the origin indicated by
$b$—nonnegative when $b$ is true and nonpositive when it is false—then for every number
of steps $t$ there is a tag $b'$ such that the head position on tape $i$ after running

\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Simulation away from oracle queries]
\lean{Turing.oracleOffQuery}
\label{Turing.oracleOffQuery}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.mapState, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.mapState, Turing.FinOracleTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_mapState_of_agreeOn, Turing.OracleTM.plainEmptyOracle, Turing.OracleTM.queryTapeIdx, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_eq_plainEmptyOracle, Turing.embedEmitCfg, Turing.embedEmitTM, Turing.embedEmitTM_runFrom, Turing.oracleShadowCfg, Turing.oracleShadowTM, Turing.oracleShadow_run, Turing.oracleSide}
\difficulty{5}
Let $M$ be an oracle Turing machine with $m$ ordinary work tapes over the Boolean
alphabet, let $O$ be a language of Boolean words, and let $P$ be a Turing machine with
$k$ work tapes and state set $H$. Suppose $\iota$ is an injection from the $m+2$ tape
indices of the shadow simulation into the $k$ tapes of $P$, and $emb$ is an injection
from pairs $(q,b)$, where $q$ is a state of $M$ and
$b\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, into $H$. Fix arbitrary contents and head
positions for the tapes of $P$. Assume that, for every such pair with $q$ different from
the query state, every scanned input symbol, and every tuple of scanned work-tape
symbols, the transition of $P$ at state $emb(q,b)$ agrees with the state-renamed
transition of the shadow simulation of $M$ with the empty oracle. Let $c$ be a
configuration of $M$ on a Boolean input, and suppose its query-tape head position is
nonnegative if $b$ is true and nonpositive if $b$ is false. If the empty-oracle
computation from $c$ is outside the query state at every time $s<t$, then there is a
Boolean tag $b'$ such that the query-tape head position after $t$ steps of $M$ relative
to $O$ is nonnegative when $b'$ is true and nonpositive when $b'$ is false, and the
configuration of $P$ after $t$ steps from the encoded configuration of $c$ with tag $b$
equals the encoding of the configuration of $M$ after $t$ steps relative to $O$ with tag
$b'$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Equality of Embedded Configurations]
\lean{Turing.oracleBankCfg_eq}
\label{Turing.oracleBankCfg_eq}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.embedEmitCfg, Turing.embedEmitCfg_selected_pos, Turing.embedEmitCfg_selected_tape, Turing.embedEmitTM_frame}
\difficulty{4}
Let $m,k$ be natural numbers, let $S$ be a state type, let $x$ be a finite Boolean
input, and let $A$ be an $m$-work-tape Turing machine. Suppose $\iota$ embeds
the $m$ work-tape indices into the $k$ work-tape indices, and let $c$ and $d$ be
configurations on $m$ and $k$ work tapes, respectively, for the same input. If their
states, input-head positions, and output strings agree, and for every work-tape index
$i<m$ the contents and head position of tape $i$ in $c$ agree with those of tape
$\iota(i)$ in $d$, then embedding $c$ into the $k$-tape configuration using $d$'s tapes
and head positions for all unembedded slots, and with an empty output prefix, gives
exactly $d$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Copying a word into a blank tape]
\lean{Turing.oracleCopy_intoBlank}
\label{Turing.oracleCopy_intoBlank}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.SweepPhase, Turing.copyTM, Turing.copyTM_run_ofCfg}
\difficulty{4}
Let $k\ge 0$, let $x$ and $z$ be Boolean words, and let $src,dst$ be distinct work-tape
indices. Suppose a configuration $d$ on input $x$ is in the sweep phase, the destination
head is at cell $0$, the destination tape is blank everywhere, and the source tape
agrees with the buffer storing $z$ throughout the window from cell $-1$ through cell
$|z|$. After $2|z|+2$ steps of the copy machine, the destination tape stores $z$ and the
machine is in the done phase. At every earlier time $s<2|z|+2$, it is not in the done
phase.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Oracle host tape count]
\lean{Turing.oracleHostTapes}
\label{Turing.oracleHostTapes}
\leanok
For natural numbers $m$ and $c$, define the oracle host tape count to be $(m+2)+(c+2)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Oracle source bank embedding]
\lean{Turing.oracleSourceBank}
\label{Turing.oracleSourceBank}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.oracleHostTapes}
For natural numbers $m$ and $c$, define an injective map from the first $m+2$ tape
indices into the host tape indices by sending each index $j$ to the same index $j$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Oracle call bank embedding]
\lean{Turing.oracleCallBank}
\label{Turing.oracleCallBank}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.oracleHostTapes}
For natural numbers $m$ and $c$, define an injective map from the first $c+1$ tape
indices into the host tape indices by sending each index $j$ to index $m+2+j$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Oracle host tape slots]
\lean{Turing.oracleSlots}
\label{Turing.oracleSlots}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.oracleCallBank, Turing.oracleHostTapes, Turing.oracleSourceBank, Turing.vhostBank}
For natural numbers $m$ and $c$ with $c>0$, define a map from four slot indices to the
host tape indices for parameters $m$ and $c$. The four selected indices are the
source-bank positions indexed by $m$ and $m+1$, the final host tape index, and the
call-bank position associated with virtual host $0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Distinct designated tape indices]
\lean{Turing.oracleSlots_injective}
\label{Turing.oracleSlots_injective}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.oracleCallBank, Turing.oracleSlots, Turing.oracleSourceBank, Turing.vhostBank}
\difficulty{3}
For natural numbers $m,c$ with $0<c$, the assignment of four designated tape indices
into the host tape set of size $(m+2)+(1+c)+1$ is injective. The indices are the two
specified source-bank positions, the final host position, and the call-bank position
corresponding to the first virtual bank tape.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Oracle dispatch states]
\lean{Turing.OracleDispatch}
\label{Turing.OracleDispatch}
\leanok
Define a finite type of oracle-dispatch states with cases for booting, readiness,
bookmarking or locating either side, saving, copying, and reading. It also has restore
and depart states carrying a Boolean verdict and an optional side, and back and answer
states carrying a verdict and a side.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Oracle dispatch action]
\lean{Turing.oracleDispatchAction}
\label{Turing.oracleDispatchAction}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action, Turing.OracleDispatch}
Given a work-tape action for each of four tapes and an oracle-dispatch state $q$, define
the machine action that leaves the input head stationary, uses the supplied work-tape
actions, emits no output symbol, and transitions to $q$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Oracle dispatch machine]
\lean{Turing.oracleDispatchTM}
\label{Turing.oracleDispatchTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.OracleDispatch, Turing.oracleDispatchAction}
Define a deterministic Turing machine with four work tapes, Boolean symbols, and the
oracle-dispatch states, whose initial state is boot. Its transition table is the one
specified by the dispatch states and the scanned work-tape symbols: it updates or moves
the four work-tape heads and contents according to the boot, bookmark, origin, save,
read, restore, depart, and back cases, and otherwise leaves the tapes unchanged and
retains the current state; it emits no output symbol and does not halt in any case.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Oracle walk configuration]
\lean{Turing.oracleWalkCfg}
\label{Turing.oracleWalkCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.OracleDispatch}
Given a configuration of a four-work-tape machine on a Boolean input, a dispatch state
$q$, and an integer $p$, define a configuration by retaining the original input-head
position, tape contents, and output, setting the state to $q$, and setting the heads on
work tapes $0$ and $1$ to $p$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Oracle Walk Run]
\lean{Turing.oracleWalk_run}
\label{Turing.oracleWalk_run}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.OracleDispatch, Turing.moveInputPos_zero, Turing.oracleDispatchAction, Turing.oracleDispatchTM, Turing.oracleWalkCfg}
\difficulty{5}
Let $d$ be a four-tape configuration on a Boolean input word, let $q$ be a dispatch
state, let $p$ be an integer, let $m\in\{-1,0,1\}$, and let $t\in\mathbb{N}$. Suppose
that at every integer $u<t$, the dispatch machine, when in state $q$ with the input
symbol read from $d$ and with the work-tape heads at the positions determined by $p+mu$,
prescribes no writes, moves the first two work-tape heads by $m$, leaves the other two
stationary, and remains in state $q$. Then, for every $u\le t$, its configuration after
$u$ steps from the configuration with those first two head positions set to $p$ is the
configuration obtained by setting both positions to $p+mu$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A bookmarked point is not the oracle origin]
\lean{Turing.oracleBookmark_ne_origin}
\label{Turing.oracleBookmark_ne_origin}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.oracleOrigin}
\difficulty{4}
Let the oracle origin be the function from $\mathbb{Z}$ to
$\mathrm{Option}(\mathrm{Bool})$ that takes the value $\mathrm{some}(\mathrm{true})$ at
$0$ and $\mathrm{none}$ elsewhere. For any integers $p$ and $z$ with $z \ne 0$, changing
the oracle's value at $p$ to $\mathrm{some}(\mathrm{false})$ leaves its value at $z$
different from $\mathrm{some}(\mathrm{true})$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Oracle local configuration]
\lean{Turing.oracleLocalCfg}
\label{Turing.oracleLocalCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.OracleDispatch, Turing.oracleOrigin}
Given a Boolean input list $x$, a tape-content function $f:\mathbb
Z\to\mathrm{Option}(\mathrm{Bool})$, an integer $p$, a dispatch state $q$, an input-head
position among the $|x|+2$ positions, and an output list, define a four-work-tape
configuration in state $q$ with that input-head position and output. Its first tape has
contents $f$, its second has the fixed origin contents, and its last two tapes are
blank; the first two heads are at $p$ and the other two are at $0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Oracle ready configuration]
\lean{Turing.oracleReadyCfg}
\label{Turing.oracleReadyCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.OracleDispatch, Turing.oracleOrigin}
Given a Boolean input list $x$, a tape-content function $f:\mathbb
Z\to\mathrm{Option}(\mathrm{Bool})$, an integer $p$, a Boolean side, an argument list, a
dispatch state $q$, an input-head position among the $|x|+2$ positions, and an output
list, define a four-work-tape configuration in state $q$ with that input-head position
and output. The first tape is $f$ with its value at $-1$ erased; the second is the fixed
origin contents with its value at $p$ set to false; the third is blank except that cells
$0$ and $1$ are assigned values determined by $p$, the side, and $f(-1)$; and the fourth
contains the argument in buffer form. All four heads are at $0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Oracle return configuration]
\lean{Turing.oracleBackCfg}
\label{Turing.oracleBackCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.OracleDispatch, Turing.oracleLocalCfg, Turing.oracleOrigin}
Given a Boolean input list $x$, a tape-content function $f:\mathbb
Z\to\mathrm{Option}(\mathrm{Bool})$, integers $bookmark$ and $pos$, a dispatch state
$q$, an input-head position among the $|x|+2$ positions, and an output list, define a
four-work-tape configuration as the corresponding local configuration at head position
$pos$, with the second tape replaced by the fixed origin contents whose value at
$bookmark$ is false.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Marked oracle configuration]
\lean{Turing.oracleMarkedCfg}
\label{Turing.oracleMarkedCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.OracleDispatch, Turing.oracleOrigin}
Let $x$ be a finite Boolean input, let
$f\colon\mathbb{Z}\to\mathrm{Option}(\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\})$ be a tape, let
$p\in\mathbb{Z}$, let $s$ be a Boolean, let $i$ be an input-head position, and let $w$
be a finite Boolean output word. The specified four-work-tape configuration has state
labelled by the origin marker for side $s$, input-head position $i$, head positions
$(p,p,1,0)$, and output $w$. Its tapes are, in order, $f$; the fixed origin tape with
cell $p$ set to false; a blank tape except for cell $0$, which contains $s$; and a blank
tape.
\end{definition}

$f\colon\mathbb{Z}\to\mathrm{Option}(\mathrm{Bool})$, side bit, valid input-head
position, and output word, running the oracle-dispatch machine for two steps from the
local configuration at position zero in the corresponding bookmark state yields the
ready configuration at position zero, with empty argument word and copy state,
preserving the input-head position and output.
\end{theorem}

yields the back configuration at position $p$ with bookmark $0$, depart state carrying

with tape $0$ equal to $f$, its other tapes initialized as specified by the local
configuration, and the first two tape heads at $p$, produces the marked configuration:
its state is the corresponding origin state, tape $0$ remains $f$, tape $1$ has its

first two heads remain at $p$, and the remaining heads, input-head position, and output

configuration based on the marked configuration, with origin state for that side and
both leading tape heads at $0$, the oracle-dispatch machine reaches after exactly two
steps the ready configuration with empty argument and copy state.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Oracle departure step]

configuration in departure phase with bookmark $p$ and the head on the first tape at $p$
yields the configuration in the corresponding return phase, with that head at $p+1$ when
$side$ is true and at $p-1$ when $side$ is false; the input-head position and output
word are preserved.

\begin{definition}[Oracle phases]
\lean{Turing.OraclePhase}
\label{Turing.OraclePhase}
\leanok
Let the oracle phases be the three distinct phases: source, dispatch, and service.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[State types for each oracle phase]
\lean{Turing.oraclePhaseState}
\label{Turing.oraclePhaseState}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinOracleTM, Turing.FinTM, Turing.OracleDispatch, Turing.OraclePhase, Turing.SweepPhase}
Given a finite Boolean oracle machine $M$ and a finite Boolean Turing machine $C$,
assign to the source phase the states of $M$ paired with a Boolean, to the dispatch
phase the oracle-dispatch states, and to the service phase the disjoint union of the
sweep phases and the states of $C$ paired with a Boolean.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Oracle phase machine]
\lean{Turing.oraclePhases}
\label{Turing.oraclePhases}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinOracleTM, Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.OraclePhase, Turing.OracleTM.plainEmptyOracle, Turing.OracleTM.queryTapeIdx, Turing.copyTM, Turing.embedEmitTM, Turing.oracleCallBank, Turing.oracleDispatchTM, Turing.oracleHostTapes, Turing.oraclePhaseState, Turing.oracleShadowTM, Turing.oracleSlots, Turing.oracleSlots_injective, Turing.oracleSourceBank, Turing.seamCompTM, Turing.vhostEmitTM}
Given a finite Boolean oracle machine $M$, a finite Boolean Turing machine $C$, a proof
that $C$ has at least one work tape, and a state $e$ of $C$, define a multi-tape Boolean
machine with $(m+2)+(c+1)+1$ work tapes, where $m$ and $c$ are the numbers of ordinary
work tapes of $M$ and $C$. Its source phase is formed from the oracle source
construction and the shadow machine for $M$'s empty-query behavior; its dispatch phase
embeds the oracle dispatch machine; and its service phase copies between the specified
slots, then embeds the virtual-host machine for $C$, initialized at state $e$ paired
with true and using the done sweep phase as its seam state.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Oracle phase redirection]
\lean{Turing.oracleRedirect}
\label{Turing.oracleRedirect}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinOracleTM, Turing.FinTM, Turing.OraclePhase, Turing.oraclePhaseState}
Given a finite Boolean oracle machine $M$, a finite Boolean Turing machine $C$, a state
$e$ of $C$, a phase $i$, and a state $q$ belonging to that phase, define a partial
redirection to a phase-state pair as follows. In the source phase, redirect precisely
when the machine state is $M$'s query state, to dispatch with the bookmark state for the
current Boolean side. In dispatch, redirect ready to the source phase at $M$'s initial
state paired with true, copy to the service phase at the start of the sweep, and an
answer state with verdict $v$ and side $s$ to the source phase at $M$'s positive-answer
state if $v$ is true and negative-answer state otherwise, paired with $s$; all other
dispatch states have no redirection. In service, redirect only the state consisting of
$e$ paired with true to dispatch at read; every other service state has no redirection.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Oracle host machine]
\lean{Turing.oracleHost}
\label{Turing.oracleHost}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinOracleTM, Turing.FinTM, Turing.oracleHostTapes, Turing.oraclePhaseState, Turing.oraclePhases, Turing.oracleRedirect, Turing.phaseHostTM}
Given a finite Boolean oracle machine $M$ with $m$ ordinary work tapes and a finite
Boolean Turing machine $C$ with $c$ work tapes, where $C$ has at least one work tape,
and chosen entry and exit states $e$ and $x$ of $C$, define a finite Boolean Turing
machine with $(m+2)+(c+1)+1$ work tapes. Its state set is the disjointly tagged union of
the phase-specific state sets; its initial state is the dispatch phase's boot state; and
its transition behavior is given by the phase host machine built from the oracle phase
machines, with redirections determined by $M$, $C$, and exit state $x$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Oracle source configuration]
\lean{Turing.oracleSourceCfg}
\label{Turing.oracleSourceCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinOracleTM, Turing.FinTM, Turing.OracleTM.queryTapeIdx, Turing.embedEmitCfg, Turing.oracleHostTapes, Turing.oracleShadowCfg, Turing.oracleSourceBank}
Given a finite Boolean oracle Turing machine $M$ with $k$ ordinary work tapes and a
finite Boolean Turing machine $C$ with $c$ work tapes, let $x$ be a finite Boolean
input, let $u$ be a configuration of $M$ on $x$ (including its query tape), and let
$s\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$. The oracle source configuration associated to
$M,C,u,s$ is a configuration on input $x$ for a machine with $(k+2)+(c+1)+1$ work tapes
and state set $M.\mathrm{State}\times\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, obtained by
embedding the shadow of $u$ on side $s$, with all auxiliary tapes blank, their heads at
position $0$, and the output empty.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Oracle configuration in the source phase]
\lean{Turing.oracleStableCfg}

Let $M$ be a finite Boolean oracle Turing machine with $k$ ordinary work tapes, let $C$
be a finite Boolean Turing machine, let $x$ be a finite Boolean input, and let $c$ be a
configuration of $M$ on $x$; choose a side in $\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$. The
construction takes the associated source configuration and tags its state with the
source phase, leaving the remaining configuration data unchanged.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Oracle host simulation away from queries]

Let $M$ be a finite-state Boolean oracle Turing machine with $k$ ordinary work tapes,
and let $C$ be a finite-state Boolean Turing machine with $C.k>0$. Choose states $en,ex$
of $C$, a language $O$ of Boolean strings, an input string $x$, and a configuration $c$
of $M$ on $x$. For either Boolean tag $side$, suppose the query-tape head position of
$c$ is nonnegative when $side$ is true and nonpositive when $side$ is false. If the run
of $M$ with the empty oracle is not in its query state at any time $s<t$, then there is
a Boolean tag $side'$ such that, after $t$ steps with oracle $O$, the query-tape head
position is nonnegative when $side'$ is true and nonpositive when $side'$ is false, and
the host machine’s run from the stable configuration encoding $c$ and $side$ equals the
stable configuration encoding the configuration reached by $M$ with oracle $O$ and tag

\begin{theorem}[Oracle host dispatch simulation]
\lean{Turing.oracleHost_dispatch}
\label{Turing.oracleHost_dispatch}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.mapState, Turing.FinOracleTM, Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.OracleDispatch, Turing.embedEmitCfg, Turing.embedEmitTM, Turing.embedEmitTM_runFrom, Turing.oracleDispatchInternal, Turing.oracleDispatchTM, Turing.oracleHost, Turing.oracleHostTapes, Turing.oraclePhaseState, Turing.oraclePhases, Turing.oracleRedirect, Turing.oracleSlots, Turing.oracleSlots_injective, Turing.phaseHostTM_run}

machine on $x$, and let $T$ be a natural number. If the dispatch machine run from $c$
for $T$ steps is $c'$, the state of $c'$ is $s'$, the host construction redirects
dispatch state $s'$ to phase state $q'$, and every state occurring in the dispatch run
at a time $u<T$ is internal (that is, neither ready, copy, nor an answer state), then
the host machine run for $T+1$ steps from the phase-tagged embedding of $c$ reaches the

Let $N$ be a finite Boolean nondeterministic oracle Turing machine, $O$ a language of
Boolean strings, and $x,u$ Boolean strings. Run $N$ on input $x$ with auxiliary string
$u$ and oracle $O$. The output is the run's output if the run halts; if it does not
halt, append one false symbol to that output.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Characterization of a true choice output]
\lean{Turing.FinOracleNDTM.choiceOut_eq_true_iff}
\label{Turing.FinOracleNDTM.choiceOut_eq_true_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinOracleNDTM, Turing.FinOracleNDTM.choiceOut, Turing.OracleNDTM.initCfg, Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic oracle Turing machine over Boolean strings,
$O$ an oracle language, and $x,u$ Boolean words. The output defined from the run using
choice sequence $u$ is exactly $[\mathrm{true}]$ if and only if that run halts and its
output is exactly $[\mathrm{true}]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Language membership via choice output]
\lean{Turing.FinOracleNDTM.mem_iff_exists_choiceOut}
\label{Turing.FinOracleNDTM.mem_iff_exists_choiceOut}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinOracleNDTM, Turing.FinOracleNDTM.AcceptsWithin.mono, Turing.FinOracleNDTM.DecidesInTime, Turing.FinOracleNDTM.choiceOut, Turing.FinOracleNDTM.choiceOut_eq_true_iff, Turing.OracleNDTM.initCfg, Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith, Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith_append, Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith_of_halt, Turing.choiceBudget_le, Turing.run_take_of_halted}
\difficulty{5}
Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic oracle Turing machine over Boolean strings,
and let $O,L$ be languages of Boolean words. Suppose $N$ decides $L$ with oracle $O$
within $T(n)=a(n^c+1)$ steps on every input of length $n$. Then for every Boolean word
$x$, $x\in L$ if and only if there is a Boolean word $u$ of length $2a(|x|+1)^c$ for
which the output assigned to $N$ on input $x$, oracle $O$, and choice sequence $u$ is
exactly $[\mathrm{true}]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Oracle Choice Tape Position]
\lean{Turing.oracleChoiceSlot}
\label{Turing.oracleChoiceSlot}
\leanok
For each natural number $k$, the designated oracle-choice tape is the tape at position
$k$ among $k+2$ tape positions, indexed starting at zero.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Action with an Oracle Choice Tape]
\lean{Turing.oracleChoiceAction}
\label{Turing.oracleChoiceAction}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action, Turing.oracleChoiceSlot}
Let $a$ be an action on $k+1$ Boolean work tapes with state set $S$. Extend it to $k+2$
work tapes and state set $S\sqcup\{0,1,2\}$ by inserting at position $k$ an action that
writes a blank and moves its head one cell to the right. Preserve the input-head
movement and output, and tag any successor state from $S$ with the left injection; if
$a$ has no successor state, the extended action also has none.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Oracle choice machine]
\lean{Turing.oracleChoiceMachine}
\label{Turing.oracleChoiceMachine}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinOracleNDTM, Turing.FinOracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.answerAction, Turing.oracleChoiceAction, Turing.oracleChoiceSlot}
Given a finite Boolean nondeterministic oracle Turing machine $N$ with $k$ ordinary work
tapes, a finite state set with decidable equality, and pairwise distinct query,
positive-answer, and negative-answer states, the associated deterministic oracle Turing
machine has $k+1$ ordinary work tapes and state set $Q\sqcup\{0,1,2\}$, where $Q$ is the
state set of $N$. Its initial state and query state are those of $N$ in the $Q$ summand,
and its positive and negative answer states are $0$ and $1$ in the other summand. If the
added tape's scanned cell is blank, its transition is the oracle-answer action for a
negative answer; if that cell contains a Boolean $b$ and the current state lies in $Q$,
its transition is $N$'s transition indexed by $b$, using the other tapes as the
scanned-tape data and extending the action to include the added tape. In a state of the
other summand with a nonblank added-tape cell, its transition makes no writes or output,
leaves all heads stationary, and enters $N$'s positive-answer state when the current
state is $0$, and its negative-answer state otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Configuration with an inserted choice tape]
\lean{Turing.oracleChoiceCfg}
\label{Turing.oracleChoiceCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.oracleChoiceSlot}
Let $k$ be a natural number, $S$ a type of states, and $x$ a finite Boolean input. Given
a configuration $c$ with $k+1$ Boolean work tapes and state set $S$ on input $x$, a tape
$t$ assigning an optional Boolean symbol to each integer position, and an integer head
position $p$, define a configuration with $k+2$ work tapes and state set $S \oplus
\mathrm{Fin}(3)$ on the same input. Its state is the state of $c$ tagged by the left
injection, its input-head position and output are those of $c$, and its work tapes and
their head positions are obtained by inserting $t$ and $p$, respectively, at the
designated choice-tape slot.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Applying a lifted action]
\lean{Turing.oracleChoiceAction_apply}
\label{Turing.oracleChoiceAction_apply}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.oracleChoiceAction, Turing.oracleChoiceCfg, Turing.oracleChoiceSlot}
\difficulty{4}
Let $k$ be a natural number, $S$ a type, and $x$ a finite Boolean string. For every
action $a$ on $k+1$ work tapes with states in $S$, every configuration $c$ for that
machine on input $x$, every additional tape contents function $tape : \mathbb{Z} \to
\mathrm{Option}(\mathrm{Bool})$, every integer position $p$, and every optional state $s
\in \mathrm{Option}(S \oplus \mathrm{Fin}(3))$, applying the lifted action to the lifted
configuration built from $c$ and $tape$, with its state replaced by $s$, gives the
lifted configuration of the result of applying $a$ to $c$, with additional tape contents
still $tape$ and additional head position $p+1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Invariance of the query string]
\lean{Turing.oracleChoiceCfg_query}
\label{Turing.oracleChoiceCfg_query}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.OracleTM.queryString, Turing.OracleTM.queryTapeIdx, Turing.oracleChoiceCfg, Turing.oracleChoiceSlot}
\difficulty{4}
Let $k$ be a nonnegative integer, let $S$ be a type, and let $x$ be a finite Boolean
string. For any configuration $c$ of a machine with $k+1$ work tapes on input $x$, any
tape contents $t\colon\mathbb{Z}\to\mathrm{Option}(\mathrm{Bool})$, and any integer head
position $p$, inserting $t$ as the new work tape in the designated oracle-choice slot,
with head position $p$, leaves the query string unchanged.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[One-step simulation outside the query state]
\lean{Turing.oracleChoice_step}
\label{Turing.oracleChoice_step}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinOracleNDTM, Turing.OracleNDTM.stepWith, Turing.OracleTM.answerAction, Turing.OracleTM.step, Turing.oracleChoiceAction, Turing.oracleChoiceAction_apply, Turing.oracleChoiceCfg, Turing.oracleChoiceMachine, Turing.oracleChoiceSlot}
\difficulty{5}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic oracle Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet,
let $O$ be a Boolean oracle language, and let $c$ be a configuration on Boolean input
$x$ with state $q$, where $q$ is not the query state of $N$. Suppose an added tape with
content $T$ and head position $p$ has scanned symbol $b$. One step of the constructed
deterministic oracle machine from the configuration obtained by adding this tape to $c$
yields the configuration obtained by taking the step of $N$ on $c$ using choice bit $b$
and adding the same tape with its head at $p+1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Pause step on the choice tape]
\lean{Turing.oracleChoice_pause}
\label{Turing.oracleChoice_pause}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinOracleNDTM, Turing.OracleTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos_zero, Turing.oracleChoiceAction_apply, Turing.oracleChoiceCfg, Turing.oracleChoiceMachine}
\difficulty{3}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic oracle Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet,
let $O$ be a Boolean oracle language, and let $c$ be a configuration of $N$ on input
$x$. Suppose an added tape has content $T$ and head position $p$, with $T(p)=b$, and let
$r\in\{0,1,2\}$. From the configuration obtained by adding this tape and putting the
control in auxiliary state $r$, one step of the constructed machine yields the
configuration based on $c$ with its state set to $q_{\mathrm{yes}}$ if $r=0$ and to
$q_{\mathrm{no}}$ otherwise, while the added tape head moves to $p+1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Two-step query-state simulation]
\lean{Turing.oracleChoice_queryStep}
\label{Turing.oracleChoice_queryStep}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinOracleNDTM, Turing.OracleNDTM.fixChoice, Turing.OracleNDTM.stepWith, Turing.OracleNDTM.stepWith_eq_fixChoice_step, Turing.OracleTM.queryString, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.OracleTM.step, Turing.OracleTM.step_of_qQuery, Turing.oracleChoiceCfg, Turing.oracleChoiceCfg_query, Turing.oracleChoiceMachine, Turing.oracleChoice_pause}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic oracle Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet,
let $O$ be a Boolean oracle language, and let $c$ be a configuration on Boolean input
$x$ whose state is the query state of $N$. Suppose an added tape has content $T$, head
position $p$, and scanned symbol $b$, so that $T(p)=b$. After two steps, the constructed
deterministic oracle machine reaches the configuration obtained by taking one
nondeterministic step of $N$ on $c$ using choice bit $b$ and adding the same tape with
its head at $p+1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Blank oracle-choice transition]
\lean{Turing.oracleChoice_blank}
\label{Turing.oracleChoice_blank}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinOracleNDTM, Turing.OracleTM.answerAction, Turing.OracleTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos_zero, Turing.oracleChoiceAction, Turing.oracleChoiceMachine, Turing.oracleChoiceSlot}
\difficulty{3}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic oracle Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet,
let $O$ be an oracle language over that alphabet, and let $x$ be an input word. Suppose
a configuration $d$ of the associated oracle machine has state $q$, where $q$ is not
$N$’s query state, and the extra choice tape is blank at its head position. Then one
step relative to $O$ leaves the tapes and head positions unchanged, sets the state to
the halting state, and appends the Boolean symbol false to the output.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Halting of the oracle choice machine]
\lean{Turing.oracleChoice_exhaust}
\label{Turing.oracleChoice_exhaust}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinOracleNDTM, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom, Turing.OracleTM.step, Turing.OracleTM.step_of_qQuery, Turing.oracleChoiceCfg, Turing.oracleChoiceMachine, Turing.oracleChoiceSlot, Turing.oracleChoice_blank}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic oracle Turing machine over the Boolean
alphabet, let $O$ be a language of Boolean strings, and fix an input $x$ and a
configuration $c$ of $N$ on $x$. Let $tape$ assign an optional Boolean symbol to each
integer cell, and let $p$ be an integer such that cell $p$ is blank. Then, starting from
the configuration obtained by adding this tape with its head at $p$, the oracle choice
machine built from $N$ halts after some $s \le 2$ steps. Its output at that time is
$c$'s original output if $c$ is already halted, and otherwise is the original output
followed by the Boolean symbol $false$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Halting simulation with bounded time]
\lean{Turing.oracleChoice_run}
\label{Turing.oracleChoice_run}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinOracleNDTM, Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith, Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith_of_halt, Turing.OracleNDTM.stepWith, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_add, Turing.oracleChoiceCfg, Turing.oracleChoiceMachine, Turing.oracleChoice_exhaust, Turing.oracleChoice_queryStep, Turing.oracleChoice_step}
\difficulty{5}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic oracle Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet,
let $O$ be a Boolean oracle language, and let $x$ and $u$ be Boolean words. For any
configuration $c$ of $N$ on input $x$, suppose an added tape with content $T$ and head
position $p$ satisfies $T(p+i)=u_i$ when $i$ is a nonnegative integer less than the
length of $u$, and is blank otherwise. Then there is a time $s\le 2|u|+2$ at which the
constructed deterministic oracle machine, started from the configuration formed by
adding this tape to $c$, has halted; its output is the output of the run of $N$ on $c$
using choice word $u$ if that run has halted, and otherwise is that output followed by
the Boolean symbol false.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Initial configuration with an oracle choice tape]
\lean{Turing.oracleChoice_initial}
\label{Turing.oracleChoice_initial}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinOracleNDTM, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.OracleNDTM.initCfg, Turing.oracleChoiceCfg, Turing.oracleChoiceMachine, Turing.oracleChoiceSlot}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic oracle Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet,
and let $x$ and $u$ be Boolean words. The initial configuration of the deterministic
machine obtained by adding a choice tape, with its ordinary tapes initialized as blank
and the added tape initialized to store $u$, is the configuration formed from the
initial configuration of $N$ on input $x$ by adding a tape storing $u$ with its head at
cell $0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Deterministic simulation of choice output]
\lean{Turing.FinOracleNDTM.exists_choiceTM}
\label{Turing.FinOracleNDTM.exists_choiceTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinOracleNDTM, Turing.FinOracleNDTM.choiceOut, Turing.FinOracleTM, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.OracleNDTM.initCfg, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_add, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_of_halt, Turing.oracleChoiceCfg, Turing.oracleChoiceMachine, Turing.oracleChoiceSlot, Turing.oracleChoice_initial, Turing.oracleChoice_run}
\difficulty{4}
For every finite-state nondeterministic oracle Turing machine $N$ over Boolean strings,
there exist a finite-state deterministic oracle Turing machine $M$ over Boolean strings
and an ordinary work-tape index $j$ of $M$ such that, for every oracle language $O$ and
Boolean words $x,u$, the run of $M$ for $2|u|+2$ steps from its initial state on $x$,
with $u$ stored on tape $j$ and all other work tapes blank, halts and outputs exactly
the output assigned to $N$ from choice sequence $u$ on input $x$ with oracle $O$.
\end{theorem}
